answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a long-lived record outside itself: a code repository with months of real commits, a domain with public history, a paid account with a past. A farm can mint a thousand on-chain identities in an afternoon, but it cannot fake a thousand basalt-solid histories overnight — each fake needs its own vault of real past work, and the signal of a genuine record is that it predates the farm. Buying aged histories gets pricier with every fake, so cloning stops paying.
